items.title: Decide when & where to host
description: Find a day and time that works for you and will work for others too. Then book a room on campus that can accommodate everyone.
If you're expecting more than 5 people, you'll want to get a room with a projector so not everyone is crowded around a laptop.
items.brainstormQuestion: How big of a room will I need and what time should I book it for?

inputs.label: Date and time for your event

items.title: Lock in your presenters
description: Now that you know the logistics of your event, it's time to reach out. Think about friends or peers who'd be excited to share how they're using ChatGPT.
Confirm they're willing and able to present—five presenters is the sweet spot.
items.brainstormQuestion: Who will you reach out to this week?

items.title: Create a slideshow
description: Events are easier to run when they have a clear structure. To help yours flow better, use a slideshow.
Think about how you can introduce the event, give each presenter a slide, pose your guiding question, and add whatever else you want.
There's a template below you can use to get started and customize as needed.
items.brainstormQuestion: How might I structure a slideshow to help the event run smoothly?

items.title: Invite people & promote
description: Use a tool like Lu.ma to build an event page with info and registration.
Be sure to clearly explain the purpose, format, and what students will get out of it.
Start with personal connections: invite people you know, group chats you're a part of. Then go wider—put up flyers, promote it at your club, and through normal campus channels.
There's a flyer template below you can use to get started and customize as needed.
items.brainstormQuestion: What's the best way to promote my event to people who might already be interested?

items.title: Finalize day-of logistics
description: Larger events can get chaotic—consider having a few trusted friends help you out.
Think through everything that goes into the day of: setting up the room, testing the projector, greeting people, keeping time during presentations, taking photos, and capturing what you learn.
Also think about any supplies you might need to bring.
items.brainstormQuestion: Do I need additional support or materials for the day of the event?
